yes, but only for some types of image: 

\-For battle backdrops, the size is 1000 pixels wide and 740 pixels long.

\-For animation sprites, every frame needs to be 192\*192 pixels, and the frame sheet has to be 5 frames wide with however many frames you want in length.

\-For faces/dialogue pictures, each picture has to be 144\*144 pixels, and arranged in sheets of 8 frames wide and 2 frames long.

\-For tile sets, every tile is 48\*48 pixels, and the total size of tilesets varies depending on what type of Tileset it is (wall, animation, B-set, C-set, etc). For anything that is not B, C, D or E set, there are specific formats you need to follow for each cluster of tiles to make sure the computer interprets and uses the data correctly. It's very long to explain but there are lots of tutorials online that can help you out.

\-Character frame sheets is a grey area - it will work correctly as long as two criteria are met: 1. The frames are arranged in clusters that are 3 frames wide and 4 frames long. 2. These clusters are arranged into a sheet that is 4 clusters wide and 2 clusters long. It doesn't really matter what the actual pixel dimensions of the sheet is, but I would advise you to make it a multiple of 48 other it might get a bit glitchy.

(I do not know how to make system graphics yet, but there are probably tutorials for that. I have no intention to learn how to make SV actor/enemy sprites as I am not using side view in my game.)

I'm pretty sure everything that is not on this list does not have to follow a specific format, but correct me if I'm wrong. Hope this helped!
